lines.text: Yeah, no, not really. Okay, this week I'll really do it.

flags.reason: Coach repeats the same unsolicited walking suggestion verbatim after participant already showed barriers and had not asked for it.
Coach asks about daughter's help after participant already said family cannot help (line 29 and earlier); ignores stated barriers.
Third identical push of the same advice; participant had already volunteered her own reminder strategy at line 39.
Participant says she needs this 'for my head' and wants to feel like herself; coach never explored mood or emotional wellbeing.

score.summary: The coach used good reflections and affirmations and built a concrete goal with a confidence rating and barrier planning. However, the same walking advice was repeated three times (lines 20, 38, 50) and the coach did not explore the participant's emotional cues or the family-support barriers she had already raised.
strengths: Line 10: affirms the participant's honesty about her goal progress.
Line 46 and 60: reflects her commitment and gives a clear, accurate summary with a check for missed items.
Line 54-58: uses a confidence scale and asks what might get in the way, building a realistic plan.
coaching_tips: Lines 20, 38 and 50 repeat the same advice verbatim; ask permission once and then reflect the participant's own strategies (e.g., the fridge reminder at line 39).
Line 44 re-asks about family help after line 29 already closed that option; move to reflecting the barrier instead.
Line 25 ('I need this for my head') is an emotional cue; try 'Tell me more about what you mean by that' before moving to the goal.
